items.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He said, “You take the next chorus.” I got up, and I sang Embraceable You with him.

ctx.x: We all – we’d finish our gigs and hurry up and go down to Birdland. That was our hangout after we did our shows around New York and New Jersey and whatever.

Birdland was our hangout. We would all get together and go down there and jam with Bird. One night I came down, and as I came down the step, he was playing Embraceable You. He saw me, and he knew I knew it – the song. Motioned for me to come on up. Come on up here. So I went up to the stage. He said, “You take the next chorus.” I got up, and I sang Embraceable You with him.” But I didn’t know that Columbia was going to record it. They recorded. It is on one of his old albums. That sort of upset me, because nobody…
Okay, so getting back into the time zone here. 1960s, ’3, ’4, you go back to Cleveland. What kind of jobs did you do in that period before you got this call from Joel Dorn to do . . .
